requirement: Parsing failure is not interpreted as zero or complete coverage

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: check.py -> real gd-tools test --coverage, then truncate coverage.json in half, then gd-tools coverage show / coverage report (gd-tools-cli 0.4.0 + GUT v9.7.1)

measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.truncated_coverage_show_output:
Error: [Error] Invalid JSON in coverage data file
  Cause: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 7 column 3 (char 74)
  Fix: Ensure the file is valid JSON generated by 'gd-tools coverage run'.
measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.truncated_coverage_report_output:
Error: [Error] Invalid JSON in coverage data file
  Cause: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 7 column 3 (char 74)
  Fix: Ensure the file is valid JSON generated by 'gd-tools coverage run'.
measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.finding: gd-tools' own JSON parsing correctly rejects a truncated coverage.json for BOTH consumers of that file (coverage show and coverage report): a nonzero exit code (2) and an explicit, specific diagnostic naming the exact parse failure and the file's expected provenance. Neither command silently falls back to 0% or 100% coverage, and neither crashes with an unhandled traceback -- this is a clean pass, not a defect, for the exact failure mode pilot/harness/comparator.py's MalformedReportError was independently built to guard against at the harness level (see pilot/harness/self_test.py's test_truncated_json_rejected).

notes: Real, verified positive finding: gd-tools 0.4.0 handles a truncated/malformed coverage.json robustly and explicitly on its own, for both places that read the file. This closes the loop between the harness's own synthetic guarantee (comparator.py refuses to interpret malformed report bytes as any coverage number, tested in self_test.py with a hand-built truncated string) and gd-tools' actual behavior against a REAL coverage.json produced by a REAL test run, truncated the same way a killed-mid-write process would leave it. The truncation point (half the file's bytes) was chosen to guarantee invalid JSON, confirmed via json.loads() raising JSONDecodeError before ever invoking gd-tools, so a pass here can't be explained by the truncation accidentally still being valid.
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
ambiguities: Only mid-object truncation (cutting the file in half) is tested. Other malformed forms -- valid JSON with a wrong top-level shape, valid JSON with wrong types for expected fields, an empty file, or binary garbage -- are not tested here and could plausibly hit a different code path in gd-tools' loader.
